items.title: Joe Bushkin interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 15, 1999
items.q: But at the Embers we did have Roy Eldridge and the group, and Teddy Wilson and the group, and Red Norvo.

ctx.x: You mean for the audience, if their bill was 20 bucks, there was a 20 percent tax on that as the war tax? © Hamilton College Jazz Archive -8-

Right. But there was no tax for instrumental groups. So if a guy showed up with a party of six or eight and racked up a tab for a C note or whatever, that twenty dollars took care of the waiter’s tip and the cab ride. And so we did a lot of business, based on the fact that during the 26 week scene, we had Red Norvo’s trio and my group. I was there for the whole 26 weeks and whatever you want to call it, I was considered the draw in the place. And then we had Teddy Wilson and a group, and actually that was a…

items.title: 66600_Teddy Wilson oral history interview
items.q: Bunny Berigan had a small group there with Joe Bushkin on piano

ctx.x: Oh yeah. Ralph Watkins. Was he....?

No, that was before Ralph. I'm going back to about 1934-35 now, and I was the house piano player there; I used to play solo there at intermissions, and Louie Prima was there for awhile and Bunny Berigan had a small group there with Joe Bushkin on piano, and Wingy Manone's little band was in there while the period I played with them -- I played intermissions, rather.

And then, from there, I got a call from Goodman -- Goodman had become a bandleader during 1935 and with a regular show sponsored by the National Biscuit Company, a three-hour radio program, and when that went off the air, he kept the band together, because the band was only organized for the radio, but he kept it together and they performed at the Billy Rose Music Hall in New York, and then he took the band on the road. And the backbone of the writing was Benny Carter and Fletcher Henderson in those days. That…
